title: Generator Runtime Engine — System Overview
description: A spec in, working software out: the engine renders templates, writes a project, executes it with node, and runs its tests.
body: The Generator + Runtime Engine is the system's builder. It accepts a structured specification — a name, typed fields, file templates with {{placeholders}}, and test declarations — validates it, renders every template, writes a real project directory, executes the entry file with node, and runs the declared tests. The demonstration is the engine's own demo cycle on a temperature-converter spec: files written, program executed (212F = 100.00C), two tests passed, verification status tested. Every number in the output was produced by running code, not by writing about code.

title: Specification Schema — What the Engine Accepts
t: Specification Schema — What the Engine Accepts
description: A spec needs a name, file templates, and optionally typed fields and test declarations.
body: The contract is small on purpose. name is required and must be lowercase letters, digits, and dashes. fields declare typed inputs (string, number, boolean). templates is the required heart: an array of {file, template} pairs. tests declare commands plus expected output substrings. Placeholders available inside templates are {{name}}, {{description}}, and {{field:<name>}}. The demonstration prints the schema from the running engine.

title: Validation Rejects Bad Specs Before Anything Is Built
t: Validation Rejects Bad Specs Before Anything Is Built
description: Malformed specifications are refused with explicit errors — nothing is generated from a broken spec.
body: Garbage in is refused, not built. The demonstration validates a spec with an illegal name, an unknown field type, and no templates; the engine returns three precise errors and generates nothing. This is the same gate the master coordinator passes through before the generator stage runs.

title: Template Engine — {{placeholders}} Become Real Code
description: Templates substitute {{name}}, {{description}}, and typed {{field:name}} markers deterministically.
body: The renderer is deliberately simple: exact string substitution, no hidden magic, so generated code is always traceable to the spec that produced it. The demonstration renders a template against a sample spec and prints the result — the same function the generate() path calls for every file.

var v = Number; // a demo

title: File Generation — Specs Become Project Directories
t: File Generation — Specs Become Project Directories
description: generate() writes every templated file into a fresh directory and refuses to overwrite an existing one.
body: Generation is a filesystem act: the engine creates the output directory, renders each template, writes the files, and returns the file list. It refuses to write into an existing directory, so a build can never silently clobber previous work. The demonstration generates a greeter project and lists the real files written.

title: Runtime Execution — Generated Code Actually Runs
t: Runtime Execution — Generated Code Actually Runs
description: runProject() executes the generated entry file with node and captures exit code, stdout, and stderr.
body: A generated program that never runs is a text file with ambitions. The engine spawns node on the generated entry, enforces an 8-second timeout, and captures everything the program prints. The demonstration runs the greeter generated moments ago and prints the captured result — real process execution, exit code 0.

title: Test Execution — Declared Tests Run Against Real Output
t: Test Execution — Declared Tests Run Against Real Output
description: Tests are commands plus expected output; a test passes only if the program exits 0 and prints what was expected.
body: Each test declaration names a command like "node main.js 212" and an expected substring. The engine runs the command inside the project directory and checks both the exit code and the output. The demonstration runs the temperature-converter's own test suite from the built-in demo spec and prints per-test pass results.

title: Limits and Honest Boundaries
description: The engine generates JavaScript for node only; it cannot compile other languages, reach the network, or invent capabilities.
body: Plain limits. Today the only runtime is node and the only output language is JavaScript — a spec asking for a compiled C++ binary or a phone app would fail validation of expectations, not quietly produce something else. Templates are dumb string substitution, so the engine cannot fix a logically broken spec; the lab exists to catch that. The demonstration attempts a spec with an unsupported field type and shows the honest rejection.

demo.output: {"ok":false,"errors":["fields[0].type must be one of string, number, boolean"]}

title: Integration — Generator Output Feeds the Verification Lab
t: Integration — Generator Output Feeds the Verification Lab
description: The lab verifies what the engine builds: this record runs the real handoff the master performs.
body: Integration is proven by doing it. The demonstration requires the generator, builds the built-in temperature-converter spec into a fresh directory, then requires the verification lab and runs its full verifyProject() on that directory — syntax, run, and tests — printing the lab's real verdict. This is exactly the generator→lab handoff inside the master coordinator's pipeline.

title: Verification Ladder — proposed, generated, executable, tested
t: Verification Ladder — proposed, generated, executable, tested
description: A spec climbs the ladder only by passing gates: generated on write, executable on clean run, tested on passing tests.
body: The engine assigns status mechanically. A spec that validates is proposed. Files written: generated. Entry runs with exit 0: executable. Declared tests all pass: tested. Nothing is promoted on promise. The demonstration runs the full build (tested, because the demo spec's tests pass) and a files-only generate (generated) — printing both earned statuses from the live code.
